sent_to_model:
Just finished a run of nights and Kiran's email was waiting for me. Reply to it on the family thread for me please. I'm genuinely thrilled Amma and Appa are coming and I don't want that to get lost, but he has a fair point about not being asked and I'd rather own that than argue. His worries about Appa's heart deserve a proper answer, not a brush-off. Everyone reads these, including Appa, so nothing that sounds like the two of us squabbling over them. Please also suggest the Sunday call and offer the Pune flights, and answer the other worries using my notes.

- visa is the UK long-term visitor one, max 6 months per visit; plan is first week of April to end of September 2027
- got them travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, about 640 GBP each for the six months, agent says covers the stent
- Dr. Prakash agreed to do Appa's review in March before they fly and a video consult in July, happy to share notes with me
- annexe at the back is finished, ground floor, no steps, own shower with grab rail
- Leicester Royal is 15 min from our house, I know half the cardiology team
- idea came from Appa, not me, on the phone in August when Rohan showed him the vegetable patch on video, he said "I could grow drumsticks there"
- Anika has made a laminated welcome timetable including "Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays"
- I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements; I should have looped Kiran in then
- Kiran is right I should have told him earlier, that's on me
- Amma's six-week thing is fair, but she can go home any time, return ticket is flexible
- Ganesh Chaturthi - they could fly Leicester to Pune for it in September and finish the trip there, or the Pune lot come here in August
- Kiran to feel heard not managed
- suggest family video call this Sunday, 4pm UK / 9.30pm India
- offer to cover the Pune family's flights for an August visit

Thread: Re: Our plan for next year
(I'm Meera Raghavan here. I'm replying to Kiran Raghavan's message of 2026-11-08T22:58:00.)

---

From: S. Raghavan (Appa) | 2026-11-07T07:42:00
Dear Meera, Kiran, Divya and all,

Amma and I have been discussing this for some weeks and we have now decided. From next year we will spend the summer months with Meera in Leicester and the rest of the year here in Bangalore as usual. Meera has started preparing our long-term visitor visa application with the agent, ready to submit in January. If all is well we will fly in the first week of April and return end of September, before the Bangalore rains finish.

We are not selling the flat. Lakshmi will continue to come for the cleaning and Venkatesh will collect the rent from the shop downstairs.

We wanted to tell everybody together so there is no confusion. Amma says she will carry her own pickles, so Meera need not worry.

With blessings,
Appa

---

From: Divya Raghavan | 2026-11-07T10:15:00
Oh this is lovely news!! Anika and Rohan are going to lose their minds. Amma please also carry the murukku achu, I have been trying to find one in Pune for ages and if you are going to be in England with Meera's big kitchen you have no excuse.

Kiran is travelling till Sunday, he will reply separately.

Love,
Divya

---

[the message I'm replying to] From: Kiran Raghavan | 2026-11-08T22:58:00
Appa, Amma,

I am happy for you if this is what you want. But I have to say this came as a surprise to me and I would have liked to be asked before the visa paperwork was already under way. Meera, I'm assuming this has been in discussion for some time between you and them.

My concerns, and I'm putting them plainly so nobody says later I didn't:

1. Appa's heart. His angioplasty was only last year. Dr. Prakash knows his case, and from what I understand visitors don't get free NHS treatment. What happens if something happens over there?
2. Six months is a long time for Amma away from her own house and her own people. She hasn't stayed anywhere longer than six weeks since Paati died.
3. We were planning to have them in Pune for Ganesh Chaturthi next year. Now that is gone.

I'm not trying to spoil anything. I just think this needed more discussion than an email on a Saturday morning.

Kiran

(About me: emergency-medicine doctor, 42, Leicester, England. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

Addresses cardiac care and insurance, Amma returning early and the competing Pune festival plans.
